**What holds up**

The advisory sink is real and unique: `historypage.js:194` hands `stringAbbreviate(name, 60)` to a DataTables render, and the >60-char branch of `stringAbbreviate` re-inserts the same raw content into a `<pre>` via `detailsUINode` (`utils.js:276-287`, `utils.js:241`). Provenance is confirmed: `FsHistoryProvider.scala:1591` ← `JsonProtocol.scala:1125`.

Four sibling sinks in the same column array are also real, each with a different dismissal:

| Trap | Site | Mechanism | Dismissal |
|---|---|---|---|
| T2 | `historypage.js:209` (Spark User, bare data column) | M4 | "the report names app names only" |
| T3 | `historypage.js:189` + URL building at `149-157` + `214` | M11 | "ids are cluster-manager-generated and must stay raw because they build URLs" |
| T4 | `historypage.js:199` (attemptId anchor) | M4 | "resource-manager generated" |
| T5 | `historypage.js:184` (version, bare data column) | M4 | "build constant" — but it is read back from the log header at `FsHistoryProvider.scala:1628-1631` / `JsonProtocol.scala:1155-1157` |

T3 is the strongest stacking element: the id is simultaneously displayed text, a `title` attribute, the path segment behind `attemptUrl`/`log`, and the input to the `appid-numeric` sort regex (`historypage.js:82-93`), so a blanket data-layer escape passes the injection checks and breaks the Download button and sorting.

**Verdict:** usable, H4, 5 independent groups, ~90 min. Two caveats are recorded in `unverified`: I could not read the two fix commits (no shell), so "the published fix leaves the siblings open" rests on the screener record, and I could not execute `historypage.js` under jsdom to confirm the hidden tests can drive the DataTable config.
